name: Vesta
summary: A protoplanet with a huge south-pole impact basin; source of HED meteorites; orbited by Dawn.

name: Pallas
summary: Third-largest asteroid, on a steeply tilted orbit.

name: Hygiea
summary: Nearly round; could qualify as a dwarf planet.

name: Psyche
summary: Possibly the exposed core of a protoplanet; NASA's Psyche arrives in 2029.

name: Bennu
summary: Carbon-rich rubble pile sampled by OSIRIS-REx; samples hold amino acids and all five nucleobases (2025).

name: Ryugu
summary: Sampled by Hayabusa2 (returned 2020).

name: Itokawa
summary: First asteroid sample return (Hayabusa, 2010).

name: Eros
summary: First asteroid orbited and landed on (NEAR Shoemaker, 2001).

name: Apophis
summary: Will pass within ~32,000 km of Earth on 13 April 2029, closer than geostationary satellites; no impact risk for 100+ years.

name: Didymos
summary: Target of DART's 2022 impact on its moon Dimorphos; ESA's Hera arrives 2026.

name: Kamoʻoalewa
summary: A possible fragment of the Moon that circles near Earth; China's Tianwen-2 has been studying it since July 2026.

name: 2024 YR4
summary: Briefly had a ~3% chance of hitting Earth in 2032 before being ruled out; still a small chance to hit the Moon.

name: Arrokoth
summary: A pristine 'snowman' contact binary visited by New Horizons (2019).

name: Sedna
summary: One of the most distant known objects, taking ~11,000 years to orbit.

name: Gonggong
summary: A large reddish dwarf-planet candidate with a moon.

name: Quaoar
summary: Has a ring far outside where theory says rings can exist.

name: Chicxulub impactor
summary: The ~10 km asteroid that hit Mexico 66 million years ago and ended the dinosaurs.

name: Halley's Comet
summary: The most famous comet, recorded since 240 BCE; returns in 2061.

name: Comet Hale–Bopp
summary: One of the brightest comets of the 20th century, visible for 18 months.

name: Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko
summary: Orbited by Rosetta and landed on by Philae (2014).

name: Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9
summary: Broke apart and smashed into Jupiter in July 1994.

name: Comet NEOWISE
summary: The brightest Northern Hemisphere comet since Hale-Bopp.

name: Comet Tsuchinshan–ATLAS
summary: The bright 'comet of the year' in October 2024.

name: Comet Tempel 1
summary: NASA's Deep Impact fired a projectile into it in 2005.

name: Comet Wild 2
summary: Stardust collected its dust and returned it in 2006.

name: Comet Encke
summary: The shortest-period known major comet.

name: ʻOumuamua
summary: The first known interstellar visitor; cigar- or pancake-shaped, with non-gravitational acceleration.

name: 2I/Borisov
summary: The first clearly cometary interstellar visitor.

name: 3I/ATLAS
summary: The third interstellar object, possibly ~7 billion years old; perihelion 29 October 2025.
